faqs.question: What does VZV IgM Antibody by CLIA - Serum measure?
faqs.answer: This test detects Varicella-zoster virus (VZV) IgM antibodies in your serum.

faqs.question: Why is the VZV IgM Antibody test done?
faqs.answer: • To check whether a person has IgM antibodies to VZV either from past varicella disease or vaccination • To assess whether a person has active immunity against VZV after vaccination or natural infection • To help monitor the progression of VZV infections

faqs.question: When is the VZV IgM Antibody test recommended, and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: Your doctor might recommend this test if you have • symptoms suggestive of chickenpox or shingles, • a history of varicella infection or vaccination and are at risk of reactivation, • complications from previous varicella-zoster virus infection, or • immunosuppression and are at risk of severe varicella disease.

faqs.question: What if the results of the VZV IgM Antibody test are abnormal?
faqs.answer: Elevated levels of VZV IgM antibodies often indicate a recent or current VZV infection.

faqs.question: What to expect during the VZV IgM Antibody Serum test?
faqs.answer: • A healthcare professional will collect 3 mL of your blood from a vein in your arm using a needle. • They will send the sample to a laboratory for testing.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the VZV IgM Antibody test?
faqs.answer: • Tell your doctor if you have received any blood transfusions, immunoglobulin therapy, or other injections within the last three months. • Inform your doctor if you have any specific requirements.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with the VZV IgM Antibody test?
faqs.answer: • Varicella-zoster virus DNA polymerase chain reaction (PCR) to detect viral DNA in skin lesions. • Varicella-zoster virus culture to isolate and identify the virus from skin lesions. • Varicella-zoster virus IgG antibody by CLIA to check immunity to VZV

faqs.question: What is the VZV IgM Antibody by CLIA - Serum also known as?
faqs.answer: VZV IgM or Varicella Zoster Virus IgM Antibody test

faqs.question: What is the varicella-zoster virus (VZV)?
faqs.answer: Varicella-zoster virus (VZV) is a herpesvirus that causes two distinct illnesses: chickenpox, a contagious childhood infection typically causing blisters and fever; and shingles, a painful rash that can occur in adults after reactivation of VZV from the dormant state in nerve cells.
